subject: POC traffic consumption metrics & owner assignments — Qorex trial
messages:
From: Chloe Martin <chloe.martin@redwood.com>
To: Emma Li <emma@qorex.com>, platform@qorex.com
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 28 Jun 2027 15:10:00 -0700
Subject: POC traffic consumption metrics & owner assignments — Qorex trial

Emma / Qorex platform team — thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we can lock the trial plan and success criteria. I’ve attached a simple traffic matrix and a sample prompt set for your review.

Key intake items from our discussion (please correct if I missed anything):
- Primary integration: API-first (agent calls platform endpoints, we act as tokenized LLM).
- Peak concurrent users: ~120 during business hours, with a planned weekend batch ingest of ~10k docs (one-time).
- Typical request pattern: 1–2 prompts per user session; immediate generation with average model response length around 120–180 tokens (median ~140 tokens).
- Burst behavior: expected short spikes up to 600 RPS for ~30–90s during product launches; baseline steady-state of ~45 RPS.
- Concurrency: endpoints will see roughly 40–80 concurrent connections; multi-tenant routing per customer ID.
- Latency target: p95 generation under 450ms for trimmed prompts (our suggestion) — Qorex indicated tolerance up to 700ms for peak bursts.
- Data sensitivity: PII occasionally present in prompts; SOC2 evidence requested (we will share controls).

Proposed POC success metrics (draft):
- Functional: 95% of baseline session requests succeed with coherent generation and no runtime errors.
- Performance: sustain 45 RPS steady-state with p95 < 450ms and survive 600 RPS spike without >5% error uplift.
- Cost: keep per-1000-token cost within the estimate in the attached calc.
- Telemetry: end-to-end traces and per-token cost visibility available in POC console.

Owners (Redwood):
- Integration/telemetry: Dev Patel (dev.patel@redwood.com)
- Throughput/benchmarking & kernel selection: Aditya Rao (aditya.rao@redwood.com)
- Program lead / timeline & SOW: Chloe Martin (chloe.martin@redwood.com)

Next actions / timeline:
1) Qorex to confirm traffic matrix + mark any adjustments to token lengths by EOD Wed (2027-06-30).
2) Redwood to provision trial cluster (dedicated capacity) and share telemetry link by Fri (2027-07-02).
3) First ingestion run (sample batch and 30m spike test) w/c 2027-07-05.
4) Readout & success signoff w/c 2027-07-12.

Attachments: qorex_poc_traffic_matrix.xlsx, qorex_sample_prompts.txt (sample prompts + expected reply lengths), signed MOA (we have the DocuSign reference below).

If that looks good, Emma, can you confirm the baseline RPS/concurrency numbers and whether the weekend batch is a hard requirement for the first run?

Thanks — Chloe
Chloe Martin
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
chloe.martin@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0192

From: Emma Li <emma@qorex.com>
To: Chloe Martin <chloe.martin@redwood.com>
Cc: platform@qorex.com, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 28 Jun 2027 16:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: POC traffic consumption metrics & owner assignments — Qorex trial

Chloe — thanks for the write-up, very clear. Confirming the numbers from our side with two small clarifications:

- Baseline: our internal telemetry shows ~50 RPS across the integration surface right now (we’ll mark 50 as baseline).
- Burst: 600 RPS is close to our expected upper bound; we can tolerate brief spikes to 700 RPS for 20–45s for marketing-driven events.
- Token lengths: 90% of responses are <= 160 tokens; we have an internal outlier set (~2%) that can be 350–500 tokens (long-form summaries). We should test both.
- Weekend batch: not required in week 1 — we can move that to week 2 if needed. It’s helpful for evaluating cold-cache throughput but not blocking.

We’ve attached a small sample of real prompts (anonymized) — the file you referenced. Also confirming the MOA was signed; DocuSign link is valid.

Questions for Redwood:
- Can the trial cluster be configured to cap long-form outputs (350+ tokens) to a separate node pool so we can measure cost/latency separately?
- For telemetry, can we get token-level cost broken out per customer ID in the readout?

Emma
Head of Platform, Qorex Inc
emma@qorex.com

On Mon, 28 Jun 2027 at 15:10, Chloe Martin <chloe.martin@redwood.com> wrote:
> Emma / Qorex platform team — thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we can lock the trial plan and success criteria. I’ve attached a simple traffic matrix and a sample prompt set for your review.

From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
To: Chloe Martin <chloe.martin@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 29 Jun 2027 09:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: POC traffic consumption metrics & owner assignments — Qorex trial

Looping internal owners — thanks Emma for the confirmations. Quick internal plan before we reply with specifics:

- Dev: please draft a cluster layout that separates short-form (<=180 tokens) and long-form (350–500 tokens) workloads. Goal: isolated node pool for long-form to avoid KV cache thrash and predict cost. Deliverable: config + estimated GPU hours by Thu 2027-07-01.
- Dev & Lauren: add telemetry hooks to expose per-customer per-token cost and a p95 latency dashboard. Include a flag to route long-form to the long-form pool for spike tests.
- Aditya (me): will run initial throughput models and provide scripts to reproduce a 700 RPS 30s spike with mixed token-length distribution (90% short, 8% mid, 2% long). I’ll also prepare a short checklist for the readout.

Proposed internal dry-run timeline:
- Wed 2027-06-30: provision trial cluster (staging) and pre-load sample KV cache.
- Fri 2027-07-02: open telemetry link to Qorex (read-only).
- Mon 2027-07-05: execute baseline steady-state run + 30m stress including one 30–45s 700 RPS spike and one long-form-only 10m run.

I'll send the cluster layout and the spike-simulation script by EOD Thu. If there are capacity constraints we may need to push the spike test to Tue 2027-07-06 but I'll flag early.

- Aditya
Principal Systems Engineer, Redwood Inference
aditya.rao@redwood.com

From: Chloe Martin <chloe.martin@redwood.com>
To: Emma Li <emma@qorex.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>, platform@qorex.com
Date: Wed, 30 Jun 2027 09:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: POC traffic consumption metrics & owner assignments — Qorex trial

Emma — thanks for the quick confirmation and the prompt samples. We’ll proceed with the plan below and will mark the weekend batch for week 2 per your note. Finalizing a couple items: 

- We will expose a toggle in the trial config to route 350+ token requests to a long-form node pool; that pool will be billed separately in the trial so you can see cost delta.
- Telemetry: we will provide per-customer per-token cost and p95 latency as requested; read-only dashboard link will be shared on Fri.
- Trial cluster provisioning: aiming for Wed (2027-06-30) staging up, production-dedicated trial by Fri (2027-07-02) if no provisioning issues.

Action items for Qorex: please confirm the following by EOD today so we can provision correctly:
1) Final baseline RPS: CONFIRMED 50?
2) Long-form outlier set should be enabled in week 1 spike tests? (yes/no) — we recommend yes for a 10-minute window to capture cost impact.
3) Any additional auth requirements (IP allowlist or mTLS) — we need this to open ports and generate certificates.

If we get those, Dev and Aditya will publish the cluster config and the spike scripts by Thu EOD; I’ll follow-up with the DocuSign MOA link and the HubSpot trial record.

Thanks — Chloe
Chloe Martin
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
chloe.martin@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0192
